policy_points: Holds shares of business partners for long-term, stable relationships and sales promotion (business collaborations, licensing, IP-related transactions).
Each issue is reviewed annually by share issue against cost of capital and profitability; the board of directors approves continued holding.
Holdings were verified as of March 31, 2026, and all current holdings were confirmed to match the holding policy.
In the year, shares increased in one issue (via a counterparty shareholding association) and none were sold; no reduction commitment is stated.
Voting on policy shares examines whether proposals could damage shareholder value before voting for or against.
cross_holdings.policy_summary: Sanrio holds listed shares of companies it deems necessary for long-term, stable business relationships and sales promotion. Each issue is reviewed annually against cost of capital and profitability, and the board decides whether to keep holding it. No commitment to reduce holdings is stated.

exec_pay.notes: Figures are inferred from a flattened table: the 取締役 row's special bonus (2m) and non-monetary pay (109m) were separated from the digit string and sum to 410m against a 411m total (rounding). Its 2m special bonus is placed in performance_jpy, since it is a bonus rather than fixed pay. The 監査等委員 row (13m total, 12m fixed) and the 辻 split (fixed 140m, non-monetary 47m) are also inferred from the flattened cells. 齋藤's 169m total is 9m parent fixed pay plus 72m Sanrio, Inc. fixed pay, 69m COLA Bonus (under clawback review) and 18m perks, summing to 168m against 169m (rounding). The 監査役 row covers
policy_points: Target mix for executive directors (excluding audit committee and outside directors): base salary 50%, performance bonus 25%, performance stock 25%, so variable pay is about half of total.
Performance bonus: a 50–150% multiplier applied to a role-based standard amount, linked to consolidated operating profit and ROE, paid after fiscal year-end.

Performance stock: points granted by role each year over three-year periods; shares delivered on retirement, with a 50–150% multiplier on targets (initial period: operating profit growth, TSR, external-rating non-financial metrics) and part paid in cash equivalent.
Approved at the June 2026 AGM: up to ¥600m and 894,000 points over three years (1 point = 1 share) for eligible directors.
Nomination and Remuneration Advisory Committee, led by outside directors, reviews pay; the CEO sets individual amounts within board policy and must give maximum weight to the committee's advice.
Audit committee and outside directors receive base pay only, a monthly fixed amount set by role, tenure, peer benchmarks, company performance and employee pay levels.
exec_pay.policy_summary: Executive director pay is split 50:25:25 across base salary, performance bonus (consolidated operating profit and ROE) and three-year performance stock tied to operating profit growth, TSR and non-financial metrics; outside and audit directors get base pay only.
